# InputSelectComponent accessibility issues

Generated by accessibility-auditor. Resolve these issues before using this component in production.

## Listbox options are not keyboard-navigable

**File:** `input-select.component.html` — `<ul role="listbox">` / `<li role="option">`
**WCAG criterion:** 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A)
**Problem:** The `<ul role="listbox">` and its `<li role="option">` children only have `(click)` handlers. There is no `keydown` event handling, no `tabindex` management, and no focus movement between options. A keyboard-only user can open the dropdown but cannot navigate between options using arrow keys, nor select one with Enter or Space.
**Recommendation:** Implement full keyboard navigation for the listbox: `ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp` to move between options, `Enter`/`Space` to select, and `Escape` to close. Track the focused option with an internal signal and set `aria-activedescendant` on the combobox input accordingly (see issue below). Each `<li role="option">` that should be reachable must have a unique `id`.

## Missing `aria-activedescendant` on the combobox input

**File:** `input-select.component.html` — `<input role="combobox">`
**WCAG criterion:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)
**Problem:** The ARIA combobox pattern requires the `<input>` to declare `aria-activedescendant` pointing to the `id` of the currently highlighted option. Without it, screen readers cannot announce which option is focused as the user navigates the list.
**Recommendation:** Add `[attr.aria-activedescendant]` on the combobox input, bound to the `id` of the currently focused option. Keep it `null` when the dropdown is closed or no option is highlighted.

## `<nav>` used as dropdown container — incorrect landmark semantics

**File:** `input-select.component.html` — `<nav class="c-input-select__dropdown">`
**WCAG criterion:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A)
**Problem:** `<nav>` is a landmark element that announces "navigation" to screen reader users. A dropdown option list is not a navigation region. Screen readers will expose this element as a navigation landmark, misleading users about the purpose of the region.
**Recommendation:** Replace `<nav>` with a `<div>` (or `<section>` with a descriptive `aria-label` if a landmark is intentional). The listbox semantics are already provided by the `<ul role="listbox">` inside it.

## Inline variant button has no accessible name when no option is selected

**File:** `input-select.component.html` — `<button>` in the `@else` branch (inline variant)
**WCAG criterion:** 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)
**Problem:** In the `inline` variant the trigger is a `<button>` containing `<span>{{inputRefText}}</span>` and a decorative icon with `aria-hidden="true"`. When no option has been selected yet `inputRefText` is empty, leaving the button without any accessible name. Screen readers will announce it as an unlabeled button.
**Recommendation:** Bind `[attr.aria-label]` on this button to the `title()` input value (which serves as the placeholder/label) so the button always has an accessible name regardless of selection state.

## Native `<select>` hidden with `opacity: 0` remains in the accessibility tree

**File:** `input-select.component.scss` — `::ng-deep select { opacity: 0; z-index: -1; }`
**WCAG criterion:** 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A)
**Problem:** The projected `<select>` is visually hidden using `opacity: 0` and `z-index: -1` but is not removed from the accessibility tree (`display: none` or `visibility: hidden` are not applied). Some screen readers will expose both the native `<select>` and the custom ARIA combobox UI, causing duplicated interaction points and confusing announcements.
**Recommendation:** Add `visibility: hidden` (or `display: none` if focus management allows) to the projected `<select>` so it is removed from the accessibility tree while still being readable by the component's JavaScript. Alternatively, add `aria-hidden="true"` directly to the `<select>` element inside the component's template projection handler, noting that consumers must not rely on focusing it.

## Inline variant: icon invisible at default state — keyboard users cannot see indicator

**File:** `input-select.component.scss` — `> button .c-icon { opacity: 0; }` / `&:hover .c-icon { opacity: 1; }`
**WCAG criterion:** 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA)
**Problem:** In the `inline` variant the arrow icon inside the trigger button has `opacity: 0` by default and becomes visible only on `:hover`. Keyboard-only users who focus the button via Tab receive no visual indicator that the button is interactive and that a dropdown is available, because hover styles do not apply on keyboard focus.
**Recommendation:** Apply the visible icon state on `:focus-within` or `:focus-visible` in addition to `:hover`, so that keyboard users see the dropdown arrow when the button is focused.
